why: Warm, unhurried Mandarin story-reading in a mother's voice, one of the safest and most established picks for very young listeners.
Short family bedtime stories with a calm delivery that suits a 30-month-old winding down with a parent.
Sleep-oriented fairy-tale readings in a soft voice, which is the gentle register this listener needs.
A teacher-led story show with clear, slow Mandarin and picture-book style content pitched at preschoolers.
Original picture-book stories told by a dad, short and friendly, with simple plots a toddler can follow.
A top-charting fairy-tale show with gentle narration, though a parent should skip the odd darker classic tale.
Straightforward Mandarin story-telling for young children, charting high in kids' stories.
Mum and dad take turns reading stories, a homely format that matches listening with a parent nearby.
A mother-narrated story show with a light, kind tone suitable for small children.
Cheerful, upbeat storytelling that adds some energy and playfulness to the mix without scary content.
Stories from a well-known children's theatre host, expressive and kind, though some episodes are aimed slightly older.
Light children's stories in Mandarin that add variety to the story rotation.
A public educational radio programme for children, reliably clean, with songs and simple topics, though it is pitched a little above toddler level.
Child-asked questions answered in simple Mandarin, covering the easy non-fiction side of the brief.
Friendly 'why' explanations for curious kids, weighted down because it is bilingual and conceptually older than 30 months.
A clean public-radio kids' show, kept low because much of it is in English and aimed at school-age listeners.
Gentle bilingual stories, safe in content but only partly in Mandarin, so it is an occasional pick.
Story-led science that is clean but aimed at school-age children, so it is included only lightly for variety.
